subject.title: Telegram owner commands: trusted execution mode for approval-gated actions

question: Should OpenClaw add a trusted-owner approval-bypass mode for Telegram group-origin privileged actions, and should it be a shared approval/tool policy rather than a Telegram-only boolean?
rationale: The requested behavior intentionally changes when privileged runtime, filesystem, cron, or config actions can run without a second approval, so automation cannot choose the security boundary or permanent config contract safely.

options.title: Design shared trusted-owner policy
options.body: Add a disabled-by-default policy with explicit sender, allowlisted group, tool-class, destructive-operation, audit, docs, and regression-test semantics across the existing approval stack.

options.title: Keep existing approval prompts
options.body: Decline the bypass and document that current approvals remain required for group-origin privileged actions unless the broader exec/elevated policy already disables prompts.

options.title: Add Telegram-only shortcut
options.body: Implement a narrow Telegram config, accepting faster ergonomics but higher risk of policy drift from shared approvals and elevated execution.

recommendation.title: Design shared trusted-owner policy
recommendation.body: Add a disabled-by-default policy with explicit sender, allowlisted group, tool-class, destructive-operation, audit, docs, and regression-test semantics across the existing approval stack.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans VISION-level security posture, config-surface policy, and approval-boundary ownership before Telegram or exec contributors can implement safely.
